  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:11 p.m., on Monday, February 13, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia,
Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Public Works/
Utilities Ray, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of
Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Police Chief Fraser, Director of Human Resources
Ko

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Andrade-Stadler

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES

Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council taking
action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may determine
that the title has been read.

Action Taken: On motion of Ms. PÉREZ, seconded by Ms. LEE, the City Council determined that the
titles to all ordinances which appeared on this public agenda had been read, and waived further
reading. Hearing no objections, the Mayor so ordered.

Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

1.  SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT (AQMD) UPDATE –
F2M23-16

  Mr. Michael Cacciotti, AQMD Governing Board Vice Chair, representing the cities of Los
  Angeles County, Eastern Region, will give a brief informational presentation regarding an air
  1
2-13-23
   quality update for the City of Alhambra and incentive programs for the City and the region.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion:  Councilmember MALONEY discussed the benefits of switching to
  electric powered lawn equipment and discussed the City’s upcoming Bicycle and Pedestrian
  plan and Sustainability Plan and how the AQMD could assist with those projects.

  Councilmember PÉREZ discussed the health implications of gas and pollution, discussed Mr.
  Cacciotti providing a presentation to the community, and suggested transitioning City lawn
  equipment to electric powered equipment.

  Vice Mayor MAZA thanked Mr. CACCIOTTI for the presentation and discussed getting electric
  lawn equipment on loan from AQMD to try at a City park.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the noise level difference between gas vs. electric lawn
  equipment. Mr. CACCIOTTI provided clarification.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the AQMD for their assistance with particulate matter
  by the SR-710 stub, noted that gas powered equipment is also a health hazard for the
  individuals using the equipment, and expressed interest in additional grants from the AQMD
  in the future.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

2.  RESULTS OF COMMUNITY SATISFACTION SURVEY – F2M18-35

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report and Dr. Timothy McLarney of True
  North Research, delivered a presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s Office. On
  December 14, 2020, based on Goal 14 of the Alhambra 2020-21 Strategic Plan, the City
  Council directed staff move forward with engaging a professional consultant to conduct a
  Community Satisfaction Survey. The purpose of the Community Satisfaction Survey is to
  obtain statistically reliable data to improve the City’s understanding of the residents’
  satisfaction, priorities, and concerns as they relate to services, facilities, and policies provided
  by the City. The data provides important support to the City as new strategic or budget
  decisions are considered. The City engaged True North Research to design the research plan
  and conduct the survey. This will be the second satisfaction survey pursued by the City since
  introducing the item to the 2020-21 Strategic Plan. As a result, this survey provides
  opportunity for year-to-year comparisons and statistical significance to identify changes in
  public opinion. True North is a full-service survey research firm dedicated to providing
  agencies with understanding of community perceptions, concerns, and priorities. The firm has
  conducted over 1,200 survey research studies for more than 400 cities and school districts.
  Alhambra’s Community Satisfaction Survey was broadly defined and designed to help identify:
  key resident issues; satisfaction with City services; opinions on strategic topics; satisfaction
  with communications and engagement; and other background and demographic data to
  understand needs, perceptions, and interests. Representatives from True North Research will
  present to the City Council details regarding the results of the Community Satisfaction Survey.
  The fully detailed results of the survey are featured in the final report prepared by True North
  and it is available on the City’s website at:

  https://www.cityofalhambra.org/DocumentCenter/View/4051/Alhambra-Community-Opinion-
  Survey-Report-2022

  2
2-13-23
   Public Comment:

  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, via Zoom, complimented the work done by the consultant who
  conducted the survey and discussed the need for additional affordable housing in the
  community.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ thanked True North Research for conducting the
  survey, discussed the growing interest of affordable housing, and noted that the Council will
  be using these survey results when discussing goals and priorities for the upcoming strategic
  plan.

  Councilmember MALONEY noted the big change of demographics of the respondents for the
  survey and discussed items of improvement that were highlighted in the survey. Mr.
  MCLARNEY provided clarification.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the preferred communication methods mentioned in the
  survey and noted that a lot of residents are not on social media, and many prefer to be
  communicated with via email and discussed the number of overall survey responses received.

  Vice Mayor MAZA highlighted all the hard work by City staff, discussed the work being done
  to solve the homelessness issue in the City, and discussed working with residents on future
  development in the City.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER thanked Truth North Research for their work on the survey,
  thanked City staff for their hard work, thanked Mr. MCCAMMON for his continued input, and
  discussed the age group of respondents to the survey.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the 2022 Community Satisfaction
  Survey.

3.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 AND RESOLUTION
  ADOPTING FY 2022-23 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS – F2M22-17, R2M23-10

  Director of Finance LIEU delivered a staff report and presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s Office. On May 23, 2022, the City Council adopted the FY 2022-23 Budget, which
  appropriated funds and approved revenue projections for the fiscal year. During the fiscal year,
  unforeseen financial needs and opportunities typically arise, which require City Council
  approval of recommended adjustments to projected revenues and expenditures. Staff is
  presenting a mid-year Budget review to provide a Budget update for FY 2022-23. The Director
  of Finance will provide the City Council will a high-level overview of the FY 2021-22 actual
  performance and updated budget projections for FY 2022-23. Staff is also requesting that the
  City Council approve a resolution adopting the FY 2022-23 Budget adjustments.

  Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ inquired if it was possible to see specifically what was
  creating the City’s overall revenue as this would help the Council be more intentional in actions
  with respect to community events and attracting businesses to the Downtown and Valley
  Boulevard corridor. Director of Finance LIEU provided clarification.

  Councilmember MALONEY expressed support for bringing down the unfunded liability,
  inquired about the overall reduction of revenue and increase of overall expenditures. Director
  of Finance LIEU provided clarification.

  3
2-13-23
   Councilmember LEE inquired about the natural gas increase. Director of Finance Lieu
  responded to questions.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the overall general revenue adjustment and Director
  of Finance LIEU provided clarification.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Mid-Year Budget Review and
  related reports; and, adopted Resolution No. R2M23-10 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra
  City Council adopting Fiscal Year 2022-23 Budget adjustments of the City of Alhambra, Golf
  Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra Capital Improvements Corporation, Alhambra
  Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing Authority and the Alhambra Public Financing
  Authority

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4-12)

All other items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine
and were enacted by one motion.

4.  NIB: FIRE DEPARTMENT STATION 71 WOMEN’S LOCKER/BATHROOM REMODEL
  PROJECT – F2M23-23, N2M23-15

  The women’s locker and bathroom area at Fire Station 71 is old and deteriorated. It is in need
  of a complete rehabilitation. Plans and specifications have been prepared to rehabilitate the
  locker/bathroom area with new fixtures, flooring, lighting, showers, plumbing fixtures, paint,
  wall and expanded locker area. Bids are due no later than 10:30 a.m. on March 16, 2023 in
  the City Clerk’s Office and will be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Alhambra Fire Department Station 71 Women’s
  Locker/Bathroom Remodel Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AUTHORIZE RFP: POLICE TOWING AND SECURE STORAGE SERVICES – F2M23-24,
  RFP2M23-3

  On July 1, 2016, the City entered into an exclusive agreement with Pavon Enterprises Inc.
  dba Al’s Towing for four years with automatic renewals for three additional one-year periods.
  On March 9, 2020, staff sought direction on whether to extend the existing tow contract,
  release a Request for Proposals (RFP), or establish a city towing franchise. City Council
  directed staff to release an RFP for an exclusive towing services contract at the conclusion of
  the current contract. The current contract with Al’s Towing will expire on June 30, 2023. The
  4
2-13-23
   tow service operator shall render 24-hour, 7-days-per-week towing and secure storage service
  of motor vehicles at the request of the Police Department. The service area and secure storage
  shall be within the city limits of Alhambra. In addition, the City may request roadside service of
  City-owned vehicles.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for police towing and secure storage services within the City of Alhambra; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF EMERGENCY MEDICAL EQUIPMENT FOR
  EMERGENCY RESPONSE – F2M23-6B, C2M23-8, M2M23-15

  Fire Department staff use emergency medical equipment daily to provide services to the
  residents of Alhambra. The current gurneys are 11 years old with a 7-year recommended
  useful life and the stair-pro chairs are 16 years old with a 10-year recommended use. The Fire
  Department has the opportunity to piggyback on a Public Safety Association Inc. (team up
  with Savvik) contract RFB#2019-05 for the purchase of emergency medical equipment. Public
  Safety Association Inc. bid specifications included an option for purchasing gurneys and
  stair-pro chairs, and related accessories. The contract expires June 30, 2024. Per the
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B), bidding exemption is authorized and the City may
  “piggy back” onto an existing contract of a government entity.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Stryker Sales, LLC for the replacement of two gurneys
  and three stair-pro chairs with accessories for emergency response, in an amount not to
  exceed $91,502.00; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M23-15)

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALHAMBRA PARK RESTROOM PROJECT – F2M22-66, N2M22-
  142, C2M23-9, M2M23-16

  On December 12, 2022, the City Council authorized the circulation of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the Alhambra Park Restroom Project. On January 26, 2023, the City Clerk received eight bids
  for the Project ranging from $342,930.00 (Sanz Construction Inc.) to $500,000.00 (At Your
  Service Construction & Energy Inc.). Staff reviewed all the bids and found the bid from Sanz
  Construction, Inc. is the lowest responsible bid. Sanz Construction, Inc. has the necessary
  licenses to complete the project, has worked on previous projects in Alhambra and had
  favorable reference checks.

  5
2-13-23
   Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY noted that while the improved facilities in the
  men’s restroom at Almansor Park are fantastic, they are high with respect to shorter kids. He
  asked staff to keep this in mind with respect to the upcoming restroom project at Alhambra

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Sanz Construction, Inc. for the Alhambra Park

8.  APPROVAL OF A LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON
  (SCE) FOR A STREETLIGHT EASEMENT ALONG RAYMOND AVENUE, VINE STREET
  TO ALHAMBRA ROAD – F2M13-29(B), C2M23-10, M2M23-17

  The City installed streetlights on Raymond Avenue in the area of Alhambra Park in the mid
  1990’s. In order to do this, the City entered into a License Agreement with SCE to encroach 3
  feet upon their property to install the streetlights and related infrastructure. The current License
  Agreement expires March 31, 2023. The new agreement is for a five-year term beginning April
  1, 2023 through and including March 31, 2028. There are no fees associated with the
  execution of the agreement as the use of the easement is for public benefit.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council took the following actions: (1) approved the execution of
  a Streetlight License Agreement with Southern California Edison for the use of their easement
  on the east side of Raymond Avenue from Vine Street to Alhambra Road; (2) authorized the
  City Manager to execute said Agreement between Southern California Edison and the City of
  Alhambra; and, (3) directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M23-17).

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  RESOLUTION TERMINATING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY – F2M20-33,
  R2M23-9

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 8630, the City Council can proclaim the existence, or
  threatened existence, of a local emergency when said City is affected or likely to be affected
  by a public calamity. Due to the unfolding COVID-19 pandemic, the Governor of California
  declared a state of emergency on March 4, 2020 and Los Angeles County proclaimed the
  existence of a local emergency that same day due to conditions of disaster or of extreme peril
  to the safety of persons and property as a result of the introduction of COVID-19. President
  Trump declared a National State of Emergency on March 13, 2020. The Alhambra City Council
  6
2-13-23
   proclaimed the existence of a local emergency within the City on March 16, 2020. The
  Governor has indicated he will be terminating the State declaration of emergency at the end
  of this month. The President has also indicated he will be terminating the National declaration
  in the next few months. The declaration of local emergency is no longer necessary, and its
  termination can be proclaimed by the City Council.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, via Zoom, discussed overall COVID-19 numbers in the nation, stated
  that the issue of COVID-19 is not gone even though the State of Emergency is being
  terminated, and encouraged residents to get vaccinated.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-9 entitled: Resolution of
  the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, terminating the existence of a Local
  Emergency

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A THIRD SIDE LETTER AMENDING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA AND THE ALHAMBRA POLICE
  MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION AND FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE
  ESTABLISHING AND AMENDING SALARY AND BENEFITS FOR CERTAIN EXECUTIVE
  TEAM MEMBERS AND CONFIDENTIAL EMPLOYEES – F2M23-2, C2M11-32, R2M23-8,
  O2M23-4809

  Director of Human Resources KO delivered a staff report. On January 23, 2023, Council
  approved a Side Letter amending the existing MOU between the City and Alhambra Police
  Officers’ Association (APOA) in order to provide for increased compensation and benefits to
  attract, recruit and retain sworn Police personnel. City staff meets with Alhambra Police
  Management Association (APMA) members on a regular basis to discuss recruitment,
  retention and other department matters as they arise. Most recently both parties met and
  conferred regarding the impacts of the increased compensation and benefits to APOA
  members and reached agreement on a side letter memorializing compensation and benefits
  that would extend the existing MOU from the last pay period of Fiscal Year 2022-23 through
  the last pay period of Fiscal Year 2025-26, aligning the term dates of the APMA MOU with the
  APOA MOU. The compensation and benefits provided to APMA by this third side letter is
  necessary in order to prevent compaction in the salary and benefits amongst the ranks and
  positions of sworn Police personnel. Additionally, an amendment to the existing ordinance that
  establishes the salary and benefits for Executive Team and Confidential employees is
  necessary. Section 3(V)(2) states “The Chief of Police and Fire Chief may receive additional
  salary and/or medical benefits that are granted to the Alhambra Police Officers’ Association or
  Alhambra Firefighters’ Association, respectively, to maintain parity with lower-level safety
  classifications. In addition, the Chief of Police and Fire Chief may receive additional salary
  and/or medical benefits to maintain parity between the two positions.” Furthermore, although
  the ordinance does not require the same parity be provided at the level of the Chief of Police
  and Fire Chief and the City Manager, it is recommended that the same compensation increase,
  increase to medical/health benefits and option to cash out forty (40) hours of vacation leave
  on an annual basis be provided to the City Manager also in order to avoid salary and benefits
  compaction amongst the three positions.

  7
2-13-23
   Public Comment:  None

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY emphasized the need for competitive salaries and
  expressed his support for each recommended action.

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions:

  1.  Adopted Resolution No. R2M23-8 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra City Council
  approving a Third Side Letter amending the Memorandum of Understanding between
  the City of Alhambra and the Alhambra Police Management Association and amending
  the City of Alhambra Compensation Plan, and direct staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action; and,

  2.  Declared introduced for its first reading the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4809: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council establishing
  and amending salary and benefits for certain Executive Team Members and
  Confidential Employees superseding Ordinance No. O2M21-4795 and Ordinance No.
  O2M22-4804

  which ordinance will return for a second reading and adoption at the next Council
  meeting.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
